notes: delegate-handoff is a discipline over `handoff export`/`handoff import --result` — it ships no verifier of its own, so this grader wraps setup-handoff's verify-setup-handoff.sh (environment sanity, same as run-handoff's grader) and then DRIVES the board's own installed handoff binary itself, the same produce-at-grade-time pattern register-cross-repo-graph's grader uses. `unwired` is the pre-state baseline (kind pre-state): no .agents/handoff at all, so the single environment-check expectation fails outright and the raw grade is 0.00 — the A/B delta the other four post-state cases (each 1.00 when the grader drives them) are measured against. `export-single` and `export-bundle` start from a NOT-yet-exported board (fixtures/exportable, fixtures/bundle) and the grader calls `handoff export` itself, then checks the produced brief's repo_root_commit against the isolated copy's real HEAD and that the doc was stamped delegated_to with a held lease. `import-clean` and `import-hostile` start from an ALREADY-exported board with a pre-filled brief (fixtures/returned-clean, fixtures/returned-hostile) built with `--no-claim` so no lease needed committing; the grader re-stamps each brief's repo_root_commit to the isolated copy's live HEAD before importing (isolated_git_target relocates every non-self-rooted fixture into a FRESH git init, so a brief's build-time SHA can never match — see grade.py's _restamp_repo_root docstring) except hostile-wrong-repo's, whose entire point is a mismatched identity. import-clean asserts the protocol's load-bearing invariant: status stays open and review becomes pending. import-hostile asserts each of the three hostile briefs (unfilled, wrong-repo, secret-bearing) is refused AND leaves its doc byte-identical — proven to discriminate against a write-before-refuse defect, not just a message match.

evals.prompt: This repo has no handoff board yet. Nothing to do here — this is the A/B baseline.
evals.expected_output: No .agents/handoff/ at all. Graded raw (no CLI to drive), the environment-sanity check fails outright: 0.00. This is the pre-state the four post-state cases below are compared against.

evals.prompt: Delegate the tenant-switch handoff to an external contractor.
evals.expected_output: A wired board with one open coordination handoff carrying complete Context/Where/Verify, NOT yet exported. `handoff export tenant-switch --to "Acme Contracting"` must write a brief whose repo_root_commit matches this repo's real root commit, stamp the doc's delegated_to, and hold a lease — all without changing status.

evals.prompt: Delegate the whole release-hardening bundle to an external contractor.
evals.expected_output: A wired board with an orchestrator (release-hardening) over three coordination children (auth-flow, payment-flow, notif-flow), none yet exported. `handoff export release-hardening --to "Acme Contracting"` must fan out: a cover file listing all three children, one brief per child with a matching repo_root_commit, and each child's doc stamped delegated_to with a held lease.

evals.prompt: Delegate the auth-hardening work to an external contractor.
evals.expected_output: A wired board carrying one `sensitivity: restricted` unit (key-rotation), one ordinary unit (rate-limit), and a bundle over both. `handoff export key-rotation` must be refused outright with nothing written — no brief, no lease, no delegated_at stamp — and the bundle export must be refused WHOLE rather than shipping the ordinary sibling. The ordinary unit must still export normally, and the restricted unit must still appear in INDEX.md by title. sensitivity is a handling flag, not an access boundary.

evals.prompt: The contractor sent back a result for the rate-limit-fix handoff. Read it onto the board.
evals.expected_output: A board where rate-limit-fix-handoff was already exported and its brief correctly filled in (result_status done, a real Evidence line, a Commits and PR line). `handoff import --result` must splice the reported result into the doc, stamp result_from/result_claimed/review, and leave status STILL open — import never closes anything; done stays a reviewer action.

evals.prompt: Three contractor results came back for review. Import each and see what happens.
evals.expected_output: Three already-exported handoffs whose briefs are hostile: hostile-unfilled (result_status never set), hostile-wrong-repo (repo_root_commit rewritten to a bogus SHA), hostile-secret (Evidence carries an AWS-shaped fake credential, AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE). Each `handoff import --result` must refuse with its specific message (not filled in / different repository / looks like a credential) AND leave its doc byte-for-byte unchanged — a refusal that still wrote is a failed refusal.
